CORRECTED on review: the shape is the Cliopatria 417 shape (Ordos, northern Shaanxi) plus Anding plus Guanzhong plus the part of the Cliopatria 426 shape north of 34 N, 1,340 H3 cells. The Cliopatria 426 shape also reaches 32.3 N: its 299 cells south of 34 N (the Qinling, Shangluo and the hills of the upper Han valley round Ankang, about 70,000 km2) are NOT drawn, because no page puts land south of the Wei valley in Xia. The Weibei and Longdong land north of the Wei valley (about 300 cells, about 75,000 km2, between 35 and 37 N) is kept as a bridging reading at confidence 2: Xia held Tongwan, Anding (416) and Chang'an (418) and the pages name no place between them; Cliopatria draws the corridor as Xia's. It comes with the 418 gain in the ledger, though the pages may date it anywhere between 408 and 418.

notes: Cliopatria row 'Xia' (410-438) is the Helian Xia (407-431, the Hu Xia of the Sixteen Kingdoms), not the Tangut Western Xia (990-1226, Cliopatria 'Western Xia', dossier western-xia): the two rows share Wikidata Q7427, which is the Western Xia's in the data/README, so identity.wikidata is null here rather than a wrong link; Cliopatria's Wikipedia field 'Xia' is also loose (the article is 'Xia (Sixteen Kingdoms)'). The cliopatria_names list has only 'Xia'. The shapes: 410 and 414 (91,399 and 136,426 km2) are the Ordos core, which the Bobo page enlarges in 408 and 416; 417-425 omits Guanzhong, held 418-426; 426-438 is the Guanzhong-centred shape that runs seven years past the 431 end. The infobox gives no area, so no area comparison is possible. NOT SETTLED: (1) the date of the Bobo's seizure of Chang'an (417 narrative or 418 era table); (2) the Xia page says Disestablished 431 against Ding's execution in 432; (3) the Western Qin raid of 426 is described with 'Fuhan' and 'Qifu Gangui' on the Helian Chang page, 'Nan'an' and Qifu Chipan on the Western Qin dossier's page; (4) the northern-wei dossier dates the Guanzhong gain to 427 (the Wei page), these pages to late 426; (5) the later-qin dossier dates the Ordos loss to 414, this dossier's pages to 407-408 (Ordos) and 416 (Anding); (6) 'Heavenly King' 407 versus emperor 417/418/419; (7) no vassal or tributary relations are recorded (the pages give none). Page budget: four pages of five. REPAIR (2026-10-19, after review): the 418-426 shape no longer takes the Cliopatria 426 shape whole. Its 299 cells south of 34 N (the Qinling, Shangluo and the upper Han hills, about 70,000 km2) are dropped because the Xia, Helian Bobo, Helian Chang, Emperor Taiwu, Emperor Wu of Liu Song, Liu Song dynasty and Northern Wei pages name no land south of the Wei valley as Xia's; the clip is a polygon along 34 N (the gazetteer has no 'Qinling' region), the Wei valley itself coming from the Guanzhong region. KEPT as a bridging reading (confidence 2): the Weibei-Longdong land north of the Wei valley (about 300 cells, about 75,000 km2, 35-37 N), which no page names, between Tongwan, Anding and Chang'an. ADDED from the Helian Ding page: Xia recaptured Chang'an and Guanzhong in 428 (gain, confidence 3), lost them by 430 (confidence 1, the pages give no date), and Helian Ding fled to Shanggui after the Chungu Plains defeat (capital dot 430-431). The western-qin 426 contest_end stays at confidence 1: the Western Qin page dates Chipan's worst defeat to 426 but says nothing on a Xia withdrawal. CROSS-DOSSIER: the northern-wei dossier has no 428 loss of Chang'an and no 428-430 regain; the western-jin dossier's 418 loss and 420 dissolve use the same 'Guanzhong only' reading that this repair widens to the Weibei-Longdong corridor.
